  99→def assert_canonical_state_transition(
 100→    current: Union[CanonicalState, str],
 101→    target: Union[CanonicalState, str],
 102→) -> CanonicalState:
 103→    """Return the target state when the lifecycle edge is legal.
 104→
 105→    Same-state writes are intentionally not transitions.  Callers that want an
 106→    idempotent no-op should compare the current state before invoking a reducer.
 107→    """
 108→
 109→    current_state = CanonicalState(current)
 110→    target_state = CanonicalState(target)
 111→    if target_state not in _CANONICAL_STATE_TRANSITIONS[current_state]:
 112→        raise ValueError(
 113→            f"illegal canonical state transition: {current_state.value} -> "
 114→            f"{target_state.value}"
 115→        )
 116→    return target_state

 185→def _material_value(value):

 268→        payload = json.dumps(
 269→            {"domain": "mw_protocol_v3_dependencies_v1", "field": self.dependency_field, "hashes": hashes},
 270→            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
 271→        )

 274→    @model_validator(mode="after")

 276→        hashes = getattr(self, self.dependency_field)

 279→            if not hashes or self.dependency_sha256 is not None:
 280→                raise ValueError("legacy contracts require dependency hashes and no compact digest")
 281→        else:

 283→                raise ValueError("compact contracts require a dependency digest")
 284→            if hashes and self._dependency_hash(hashes) != self.dependency_sha256:
 285→                raise ValueError("dependency hashes do not match compact digest")
 286→            object.__setattr__(self, self.dependency_field, ())
 287→        return self

 294→            else self.dependency_field, None,

 524→        if not is_derived and has_parent_identity:
 525→            raise ValueError("original artifacts must not declare parent identity")
 526→        if self.canonical_state not in {
 527→            CanonicalState.CONFIRMED,
 528→            CanonicalState.FROZEN,

1012→        if self.status is ReservationStatus.COMPLETED:

1435→        if len(claim_types) != len(set(claim_types)):
1436→            raise ValueError(
1437→                "conflicting claim obligations: a claim type cannot carry two "
1438→                "obligation entries"
1439→            )
1440→        _unique(self.project_specific_elements, "project_specific_elements")
1441→        _unique(
1442→            tuple(
1443→                item.object_kind.value for item in self.structural_object_obligations
1444→            ),
1445→            "structural_object_obligations",
1446→        )
1447→        forbidden_claims = {
1448→            item.claim_type
1449→            for item in self.claim_requirements
1450→            if item.obligation is ClaimObligation.FORBIDDEN
1451→        }
1452→        for evidence in self.evidence_source_requirements:
1453→            if forbidden_claims & set(evidence.admission_claim_types):
1454→                raise ValueError(
1455→                    "a forbidden claim type cannot be an admission requirement"
1456→                )
1457→        obligations = (
1458→            self.fact_requirements,
1459→            self.claim_requirements,
1460→            self.evidence_source_requirements,
1461→            self.structural_object_obligations,
1462→            self.project_specific_elements,
1463→        )
1464→        if not any(obligations):
1465→            raise ValueError("SubstantiveContentContractV2 is vacuous")
1466→        if (
1467→            self.structural_object_obligations
1468→            and not self.fact_requirements
1469→            and not self.claim_requirements
1470→            and not self.evidence_source_requirements
1471→            and not self.project_specific_elements
1472→        ):
1473→            raise ValueError(
1474→                "object-only content obligations require project-specific "
1475→                "elements instead of generic title/paragraph presence"
1476→            )
1477→        positive = (
1478→            any(item.obligation is FactObligation.REQUIRED for item in self.fact_requirements)
1479→            or any(item.obligation is ClaimObligation.REQUIRED for item in self.claim_requirements)
1480→            or self.evidence_source_requirements
1481→            or self.project_specific_elements
1482→        )
1483→        if not positive:
1484→            raise ValueError("content contract requires a positive substantive obligation")
1485→        return self

1488→class ChapterContractV2(StatefulProtocolV3Model):
1489→    schema_version: Literal["mw_protocol_v3_contract_v2"] = (
1490→        CHAPTER_CONTRACT_V2_SCHEMA_VERSION
1491→    )
1492→    chapter_contract_id: StableId
1493→    semantic_node_id: StableId
1494→    contract_version: NonEmptyText
1495→    template_id: StableId
1496→    template_sha256: Sha256
1497→    chapter_skill_id: StableId
1498→    chapter_skill_version: NonEmptyText
1499→    substantive_content: SubstantiveContentContractV2
1500→    word_rules: WordFormattingRules
1501→    positive_qc_rules: Annotated[tuple[PositiveQcRule, ...], Field(min_length=1)]
1502→    conditional_applicability_rules: tuple[ConditionalApplicabilityRule, ...] = ()
1503→    dependency_ids: tuple[StableId, ...] = ()
1504→    dependency_repair_policy: Optional[DependencyRepairPolicy] = None
1505→    ctq_items: tuple[CriticalToQualityItem, ...] = ()
1506→    patient_participation_obligations: tuple[PatientParticipationObligation, ...] = ()
1507→    registry_consistency_obligations: tuple[RegistryConsistencyObligation, ...] = ()
1508→    canonical_state: CanonicalState = CanonicalState.FROZEN
1509→
1510→    @model_validator(mode="after")
1511→    def validate_chapter_contract_v2(self) -> Self:
1512→        if self.substantive_content.chapter_contract_id != self.chapter_contract_id:
1513→            raise ValueError("substantive content belongs to a different chapter contract")
1514→        _unique(
1515→            tuple(item.positive_qc_rule_id for item in self.positive_qc_rules),
1516→            "positive_qc_rule_ids",
1517→        )
1518→        _unique(
1519→            tuple(
1520→                item.conditional_applicability_rule_id
1521→                for item in self.conditional_applicability_rules
1522→            ),
1523→            "conditional_applicability_rule_ids",
1524→        )
1525→        _unique(self.dependency_ids, "dependency_ids")
1526→        _unique(tuple(item.ctq_item_id for item in self.ctq_items), "ctq_item_ids")
1527→        _unique(
1528→            tuple(
1529→                item.patient_participation_obligation_id
1530→                for item in self.patient_participation_obligations
1531→            ),
1532→            "patient_participation_obligation_ids",
1533→        )
1534→        _unique(
1535→            tuple(
1536→                item.registry_consistency_obligation_id
1537→                for item in self.registry_consistency_obligations
1538→            ),
1539→            "registry_consistency_obligation_ids",
1540→        )
1541→        if self.dependency_ids and self.dependency_repair_policy is None:
1542→            raise ValueError("declared dependencies require a repair policy and owner")
1543→        if self.dependency_repair_policy is not None:
1544→            undeclared = set(self.dependency_repair_policy.dependency_ids) - set(
1545→                self.dependency_ids
1546→            )
1547→            if undeclared:
1548→                raise ValueError(
1549→                    "repair policy references undeclared dependency IDs"
1550→                )
1551→        declared_qc_rules = {
1552→            item.positive_qc_rule_id for item in self.positive_qc_rules
1553→        }
1554→        for item in self.ctq_items:
1555→            if set(item.positive_qc_rule_ids) - declared_qc_rules:
1556→                raise ValueError(
1557→                    "CtQ item references an unknown positive QC rule"
1558→                )
1559→        if self.canonical_state not in {
1560→            CanonicalState.FROZEN,
1561→            CanonicalState.SUPERSEDED,
1562→            CanonicalState.QUARANTINED,
1563→        }:
1564→            raise ValueError("ChapterContractV2 must be frozen before execution")
1565→        return self

1→"""Strict fail-closed loader for the Protocol v3 role and skill registries.
   2→
   3→See :mod:`app.protocol_workflow.registries` for the design authority and the
   4→offline discipline this module enforces.  The two public entry points are
   5→:func:`load_role_registry` and :func:`load_skill_registry`; both accept either
   6→a filesystem path or an already-parsed ``dict`` and return immutable typed
   7→documents.
   8→
   9→The registry documents are closed (``extra="forbid"`` Pydantic models).  The
  10→loader additionally applies semantic fail-closed rules that Pydantic field
  11→validation cannot express on its own:
  12→
  13→* the role registry must declare *exactly* the four product AI roles and obey
  14→  the role/thinking discipline (OCR and translation freeze effort to ``none``
  15→  and expose no thinking control; LLM and OCR/translation-support may
  16→  configure thinking/effort);
  17→* every ``allowed_efforts`` value is a member of the canonical
  18→  :class:`ReasoningEffort` closed set;
  19→* credential-shaped keys/values and path-escaping ``allowed_paths`` entries
  20→  are rejected before any object is constructed;
  21→* skill entries build canonical :class:`SkillDefinition` objects from the
  22→  representable fields and carry the remaining registry metadata verbatim.
  23→"""
  24→
  25→from __future__ import annotations
  26→
  27→import json
  28→import re
  29→from collections.abc import Mapping
  30→from pathlib import Path
  31→from types import MappingProxyType
  32→from typing import Any
  33→
  34→from pydantic import (
  35→    BaseModel,
  36→    ConfigDict,
  37→    Field,
  38→    ValidationError,
  39→    field_serializer,
  40→    field_validator,
  41→    model_validator,
  42→)
  43→
  44→from packages.contracts.workbench_contracts.protocol_v3 import (
  45→    CanonicalState,
  46→    ReasoningEffort,
  47→    SideEffectKind,
  48→    SkillDefinition,
  49→)
  50→
  51→__all__ = [
  52→    "CREDENTIAL_KEY_RE",
  53→    "CREDENTIAL_VALUE_RE",
  54→    "PATH_ESCAPE_RE",
  55→    "REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSIONS",
  56→    "RegistryDocumentError",
  57→    "RegistryLoadError",
  58→    "RoleEntry",
  59→    "RoleRegistryDocument",
  60→    "SkillEntry",
  61→    "SkillRegistryDocument",
  62→    "load_role_registry",
  63→    "load_skill_registry",
  64→]
  65→
  66→
  67→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  68→# Closed sets and credential / path-escape scanners
  69→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  70→
  71→#: Closed set of role kinds for the four product AI roles (design section 17.1).
  72→PRODUCT_ROLE_KINDS = frozenset({"llm", "ocr", "translation", "ocr_translation_support"})
  73→
  74→#: Roles whose ``thinking_configurable`` flag must be ``True``.
  75→THINKING_CAPABLE_KINDS = frozenset({"llm", "ocr_translation_support"})
  76→
  77→#: Roles whose effort must be frozen to ``none`` and must expose no thinking.
  78→EFFORT_FROZEN_KINDS = frozenset({"ocr", "translation"})
  79→
  80→#: The two thinking-frozen roles must only permit the ``none`` effort.
  81→_FROZEN_EFFORTS = frozenset({ReasoningEffort.NONE.value})
  82→
  83→#: Closed set of valid ``schema_version`` values for registry documents.
  84→REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {
  85→    "role": "protocol-v3-role-registry.v1",
  86→    "skill": "protocol-v3-skill-registry.v1",
  87→}
  88→
  89→#: Keys that smell like credentials.  Matched case-insensitively against the
  90→#: whole key.  Registry documents must be credential-free.
  91→CREDENTIAL_KEY_RE = re.compile(
  92→    r"(?i)(password|passwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key|credential|private[_-]?key|"
  93→    r"access[_-]?key|bearer|authorization)"
  94→)
  95→
  96→#: Values that smell like credentials (bearer tokens, private key headers,
  97→#: long hex/base64 secrets preceded by a credential-shaped key).  Used as a
  98→#: defence-in-depth scan in addition to the key scan.
  99→CREDENTIAL_VALUE_RE = re.compile(
 100→    r"(?i)(Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|"
 101→    r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16})"
 102→)
 103→
 104→#: ``allowed_paths`` entries must be repository-relative and must not escape.
 105→#: Absolute paths, home expansion and parent traversal are all rejected.
 106→PATH_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(
 107→    r"(^\s*/)|(^~/)|(^~$)|(\.\./)|(\.\.\\)|(^[A-Za-z]:)|(^\\\\)|\\"
 108→)
 109→
 110→#: The five ``agent_role`` values permitted by the canonical SkillDefinition.
 111→_AGENT_ROLES = frozenset(
 112→    {"coordinator", "corpus", "design_and_summary", "full_draft", "quality_control"}
 113→)
 114→

 116→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 117→# Errors
 118→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 119→
 120→
 121→class RegistryDocumentError(ValueError):
 122→    """Raised when a registry document violates the closed/fail-closed rules."""
 123→
 124→
 125→#: Alias retained for callers that treat registry load failures uniformly.
 126→RegistryLoadError = RegistryDocumentError
 127→
 128→
 129→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 130→# Credential / path scanning helpers
 131→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 132→
 133→
 134→def _scan_credentials(node: Any, location: str) -> None:
 135→    """Recursively reject credential-shaped keys or values.
 136→
 137→    ``location`` is a dotted path used only to produce a precise message.
 138→    """
 139→    if isinstance(node, Mapping):
 140→        for key, value in node.items():
 141→            child = f"{location}.{key}"
 142→            if isinstance(key, str) and CREDENTIAL_KEY_RE.search(key):
 143→                raise RegistryDocumentError(
 144→                    f"credential-shaped key rejected at {child!r}: {key!r}"
 145→                )
 146→            if isinstance(value, str) and CREDENTIAL_VALUE_RE.search(value):
 147→                raise RegistryDocumentError(
 148→                    f"credential-shaped value rejected at {child!r}"
 149→                )
 150→            _scan_credentials(value, child)
 151→    elif isinstance(node, (list, tuple)):
 152→        for index, item in enumerate(node):
 153→            _scan_credentials(item, f"{location}[{index}]")
 154→
 155→
 156→def _scan_paths(entries: tuple[str, ...], location: str) -> None:
 157→    for index, value in enumerate(entries):
 158→        if PATH_ESCAPE_RE.search(value):
 159→            raise RegistryDocumentError(
 160→                f"escaping or absolute path rejected at {location}[{index}]: {value!r}"
 161→            )
 162→
 163→
 164→def _reject_unknown(value: Any, allowed: frozenset[str], label: str) -> None:
 165→    if value not in allowed:
 166→        raise RegistryDocumentError(
 167→            f"unknown {label}: {value!r}; allowed: {sorted(allowed)}"
 168→        )

 204→class RoleEntry(BaseModel):
 205→    """A single registered product AI role."""
 206→
 207→    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, str_strip_whitespace=True)
 208→
 209→    role_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=160)
 210→    role_kind: str
 211→    description: str = Field(min_length=1)
 212→    thinking_configurable: bool
 213→    default_effort: str
 214→    allowed_efforts: tuple[str, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
 215→    target_profile: _TargetProfile
 216→
 217→    @field_validator("role_id")
 218→    @classmethod
 219→    def _stable_id(cls, value: str) -> str:
 220→        if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[._:-][a-z0-9]+)*", value):
 221→            raise ValueError(f"malformed role_id (stable id): {value!r}")
 222→        return value
 223→
 224→    @field_validator("role_kind")
 225→    @classmethod
 226→    def _role_kind_closed(cls, value: str) -> str:
 227→        _reject_unknown(value, PRODUCT_ROLE_KINDS, "role_kind")
 228→        return value
 229→
 230→    @field_validator("default_effort", "allowed_efforts")
 231→    @classmethod
 232→    def _effort_in_canonical_set(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
 233→        allowed = {member.value for member in ReasoningEffort}
 234→        values = value if isinstance(value, tuple) else (value,)
 235→        for item in values:
 236→            if item not in allowed:
 237→                raise ValueError(
 238→                    f"unknown effort: {item!r}; allowed: {sorted(allowed)}"
 239→                )
 240→        return value
 241→
 242→    @model_validator(mode="after")
 243→    def _enforce_thinking_discipline(self) -> RoleEntry:
 244→        # Thinking-capable roles must flag configurable; frozen roles must not.
 245→        if self.role_kind in THINKING_CAPABLE_KINDS and not self.thinking_configurable:
 246→            raise ValueError(
 247→                f"role_kind {self.role_kind!r} must set thinking_configurable=true"
 248→            )
 249→        if self.role_kind in EFFORT_FROZEN_KINDS and self.thinking_configurable:
 250→            raise ValueError(
 251→                f"role_kind {self.role_kind!r} must set thinking_configurable=false"
 252→            )
 253→        # Frozen roles permit only effort=none.
 254→        if self.role_kind in EFFORT_FROZEN_KINDS:
 255→            if set(self.allowed_efforts) != _FROZEN_EFFORTS:
 256→                raise ValueError(
 257→                    f"role_kind {self.role_kind!r} must freeze allowed_efforts to "
 258→                    f"{{'none'}}; got {sorted(set(self.allowed_efforts))}"
 259→                )
 260→            if self.default_effort != ReasoningEffort.NONE.value:
 261→                raise ValueError(
 262→                    f"role_kind {self.role_kind!r} must freeze default_effort to 'none'"
 263→                )
 264→        # default_effort must be among allowed_efforts.
 265→        if self.default_effort not in self.allowed_efforts:
 266→            raise ValueError("default_effort must be a member of allowed_efforts")
 267→        return self

 291→    def _exactly_four_product_roles_unique(self) -> RoleRegistryDocument:
 292→        ids = [role.role_id for role in self.roles]

 294→            duplicates = sorted({role_id for role_id in ids if ids.count(role_id) > 1})

 299→                f"registry must declare exactly the four product role kinds "
 300→                f"{sorted(PRODUCT_ROLE_KINDS)}; got {sorted(kinds)}"
 301→            )
 302→        if len(self.roles) != 4:
 303→            raise ValueError(
 304→                f"registry must declare exactly four roles; got {len(self.roles)}"
 305→            )
 306→        return self

 384→    def _agent_role_closed(cls, value: str) -> str:
 385→        _reject_unknown(value, _AGENT_ROLES, "agent_role")
 386→        return value
 387→
 388→    @field_validator("side_effect_kind")
 389→    @classmethod
 390→    def _side_effect_closed(cls, value: str) -> str:
 391→        allowed = {member.value for member in SideEffectKind}
 392→        _reject_unknown(value, allowed, "side_effect_kind")
 393→        return value
 394→
 395→    @field_validator("allowed_paths")
 396→    @classmethod
 397→    def _paths_no_escape(cls, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 398→        _scan_paths(value, "allowed_paths")
 399→        return value
 400→
 401→    @model_validator(mode="after")
 402→    def _unique_collections(self) -> SkillEntry:
 403→        for attr in (
 404→            "allowed_tools",
 405→            "allowed_paths",
 406→            "acceptance_test_ids",
 407→            "evidence_requirements",
 408→            "error_codes",
 409→        ):
 410→            collection = getattr(self, attr)
 411→            if len(collection) != len(set(collection)):
 412→                raise ValueError(f"{attr} must not contain duplicates")
 413→        object.__setattr__(
 414→            self, "tool_versions", MappingProxyType(dict(self.tool_versions))
 415→        )
 416→        return self
 417→
 418→    @field_serializer("tool_versions")
 419→    def _serialize_tool_versions(self, value: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
 420→        return dict(value)
 421→
 422→    def to_skill_definition(self) -> SkillDefinition:
 423→        """Build the canonical :class:`SkillDefinition` from the fields the
 424→        contract is able to represent.
 425→
 426→        The remaining registry metadata (applicability, idempotency policy,
 427→        error codes, prompt/tool versions, rollback) is intentionally not on
 428→        the canonical contract and stays on this entry.  The skill is frozen.
 429→        """
 430→        return SkillDefinition(
 431→            skill_definition_id=self.skill_definition_id,
 432→            skill_version=self.skill_version,
 433→            agent_role=self.agent_role,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
 434→            input_schema_ref=self.input_schema_ref,
 435→            output_schema_ref=self.output_schema_ref,
 436→            evidence_requirements=self.evidence_requirements,
 437→            allowed_tools=self.allowed_tools,
 438→            allowed_paths=self.allowed_paths,
 439→            side_effect_kind=SideEffectKind(self.side_effect_kind),
 440→            acceptance_test_ids=self.acceptance_test_ids,
 441→            canonical_state=CanonicalState.FROZEN,
 442→        )
 443→
 444→
 445→class SkillRegistryDocument(BaseModel):
 446→    """Closed, versioned skill registry document."""
 447→
 448→    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, str_strip_whitespace=True)
 449→
 450→    schema_version: str
 451→    generated_for: str = Field(min_length=1)
 452→    authority: str = Field(min_length=1)
 453→    skills: tuple[SkillEntry, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
 454→
 455→    @field_validator("schema_version")
 456→    @classmethod
 457→    def _version_closed(cls, value: str) -> str:
 458→        expected = REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSIONS["skill"]
 459→        if value != expected:
 460→            raise ValueError(
 461→                f"unknown skill schema_version: {value!r}; expected {expected!r}"
 462→            )
 463→        return value
 464→
 465→    @model_validator(mode="after")
 466→    def _unique_skill_ids(self) -> SkillRegistryDocument:
 467→        ids = [skill.skill_definition_id for skill in self.skills]
 468→        if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
 469→            duplicates = sorted(
 470→                {skill_id for skill_id in ids if ids.count(skill_id) > 1}
 471→            )
 472→            raise ValueError(f"duplicate skill_definition_id values: {duplicates}")
 473→        return self
 474→
 475→    def skill_definitions(self) -> tuple[SkillDefinition, ...]:
 476→        """Build the canonical SkillDefinition objects for every entry."""
 477→        return tuple(skill.to_skill_definition() for skill in self.skills)
 478→
 479→
 480→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 481→# Public load entry points
 482→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 483→
 484→
 485→def _load_json(source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 486→    if isinstance(source, Mapping):
 487→        # Defensive copy so the caller cannot mutate the parsed document.
 488→        return json.loads(json.dumps(dict(source), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True))
 489→    path = Path(source)
 490→    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 491→    data = json.loads(text)
 492→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
 493→        raise RegistryDocumentError(
 494→            f"registry document must be a JSON object; got {type(data).__name__}"
 495→        )
 496→    return data
 497→
 498→
 499→def load_role_registry(
 500→    source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any],
 501→) -> RoleRegistryDocument:
 502→    """Load and validate the role registry document fail-closed.
 503→
 504→    ``source`` is a path to ``role_registry.json`` or an already-parsed
 505→    mapping.  Raises :class:`RegistryDocumentError` (a ``ValueError``) for any
 506→    closed-set, schema-version, credential, path-escape, duplicate or
 507→    role-thinking violation.
 508→    """
 509→    data = _load_json(source)
 510→    _scan_credentials(data, "role-registry")
 511→    try:
 512→        document = RoleRegistryDocument.model_validate(data)
 513→    except ValidationError as exc:
 514→        raise RegistryDocumentError(f"role registry failed closed: {exc}") from exc
 515→    return document
 516→
 517→
 518→def load_skill_registry(
 519→    source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any],
 520→) -> SkillRegistryDocument:
 521→    """Load and validate the skill registry document fail-closed.
 522→
 523→    Builds canonical :class:`SkillDefinition` objects via
 524→    :meth:`SkillRegistryDocument.skill_definitions`.  Raises
 525→    :class:`RegistryDocumentError` for any closed-set, schema-version,
 526→    credential, path-escape, duplicate or stable-id violation.
 527→    """
 528→    data = _load_json(source)
 529→    _scan_credentials(data, "skill-registry")
 530→    try:
 531→        document = SkillRegistryDocument.model_validate(data)
 532→    except ValidationError as exc:
 533→        raise RegistryDocumentError(f"skill registry failed closed: {exc}") from exc
 534→    # Eagerly construct the canonical SkillDefinition objects so a
 535→    # representability gap surfaces here, not at first dispatch.
 536→    document.skill_definitions()
 537→    return document

1→"""Typed chapter registry core for Protocol v3 Task 3R.3.
   2→
   3→This module is reusable registry infrastructure only.  It loads per-node
   4→registries whose chapters embed the accepted :class:`ChapterContractV2`
   5→payloads together with dedicated chapter-skill manifests, a closed fact/claim
   6→vocabulary and executable positive/negative fixtures.  It deliberately does
   7→NOT author clinical chapter content, call any product, or decide medical or
   8→QC judgment: deterministic findings and unexecuted judgment obligations are
   9→reported separately.
  10→
  11→Compact JSON layout (documented by :func:`load_chapter_registry` and the
  12→round-trip example in ``tests/protocol_v3/test_all_chapter_contracts.py``)::
  13→
  14→    {
  15→      "schema_version": "protocol-v3-chapter-registry.v1",
  16→      "generated_for": "...", "authority": "...",
  17→      "template_id": "tp_ma_07_v2",
  18→      "template_sha256": "<frozen source sha256 of the accepted template>",
  19→      "fact_vocabulary":  ["picos.objective.primary", ...],
  20→      "claim_vocabulary": ["study_objective", ...],
  21→      "chapters": [
  22→        {"node_id": "v2_n_3_1_1",
  23→         "coverage_role": "heading_leaf",
  24→         "contract":   { ...ChapterContractV2 payload, embedded verbatim... },
  25→         "skills":     [ { ...ChapterSkillManifest payload... } ]},
  26→        ...
  27→      ],
  28→      "fixtures": [
  29→        {"fixture_id": "fixture:objectives:positive",
  30→         "chapter_contract_id": "contract:v2-n-3-1-1:v2",
  31→         "fixture_kind": "positive",
  32→         "content": {"facts": [...], "claims": [...],
  33→                      "evidence": [...], "objects": [...]},
  34→         "supplied_passed": null, "supplied_qc_verdict": null}
  35→      ]
  36→    }
  37→
  38→``coverage_role`` is one of ``heading_leaf`` (leaf in both the heading-style
  39→tree and the outlined tree), ``heading_only_aggregation`` (heading-tree-only
  40→leaf such as the TP-MA-07 appendix container: aggregation/Word obligations,
  41→not a content leaf), ``outline_only_leaf`` (glossary / concrete appendix
  42→leaves), or ``cover`` (the unheaded front-block carrier).  Coverage truth is
  43→always derived from the template ``node_tree.json`` at lint time; counts are
  44→never hardcoded.
  45→
  46→The chapter-skill manifests carry no model transport fields: provider/model
  47→choice belongs to the approved role binding (``role_registry.json``), not to
  48→an individual skill.  The skill I/O schemas are the concrete exported
  49→Pydantic types :class:`ChapterSkillInput` and :class:`ChapterSkillOutput`;
  50→manifest schema refs must name exactly those types.
  51→"""
  52→
  53→from __future__ import annotations
  54→
  55→import importlib
  56→import json
  57→from collections.abc import Mapping
  58→from pathlib import Path
  59→from types import MappingProxyType
  60→from typing import Any, Literal, Optional
  61→
  62→from pydantic import (
  63→    BaseModel,
  64→    ConfigDict,
  65→    Field,
  66→    ValidationError,
  67→    field_serializer,
  68→    field_validator,
  69→    model_validator,

 306→def resolve_schema_ref(ref: str) -> type[BaseModel]:
 307→    """Resolve a ``module:TypeName`` schema ref to the exported Pydantic type."""
 308→    module_name, _, type_name = ref.partition(":")
 309→    if not module_name or not type_name:
 310→        raise ChapterRegistryError(f"malformed schema ref: {ref!r}")
 311→    try:
 312→        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
 313→        resolved = getattr(module, type_name)
 314→    except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
 315→        raise ChapterRegistryError(f"schema ref does not resolve: {ref!r}") from exc
 316→    if not (isinstance(resolved, type) and issubclass(resolved, BaseModel)):
 317→        raise ChapterRegistryError(f"schema ref is not a Pydantic model: {ref!r}")
 318→    return resolved

1→"""Read-only stdlib assembly CLI for Task3R.3 batch chapter registries.
   2→
   3→Joins the authored per-node chapter-contract JSON files
   4→(``chapter_contracts/<node_id>.json``), their companion chapter-skill
   5→manifests (``chapter_skills/<node_id>.json``) and a batch fixture/vocabulary
   6→document (closed fact/claim vocabularies, coverage roles, executable
   7→fixtures) into one accepted :class:`ChapterRegistryDocument` shape.  The
   8→chapter JSON files stay the single authored contracts; this helper never
   9→duplicates or rewrites their content.
  10→
  11→Library model validation is mandatory: every contract payload must validate
  12→as :class:`ChapterContractV2`, every skill payload as
  13→:class:`ChapterSkillManifest`, and the assembled document must pass the
  14→fail-closed ``load_chapter_registry`` before it is printed.  Output goes to
  15→stdout only; the CLI performs no writes, no activation and no promotion.
  16→Later batches reuse this same assembly.
  17→
  18→Exit status: 0 success; 2 usage/input failure (unreadable files, schema
  19→mismatch, identity binding failure, or fail-closed registry validation).
  20→"""
  21→
  22→from __future__ import annotations
  23→
  24→import argparse
  25→import json
  26→import sys
  27→from pathlib import Path
  28→
  29→_SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
  30→_REPO_ROOT = _SCRIPT_DIR.parents[2]
  31→for _path in ("services/api", "packages", "."):
  32→    _candidate = _REPO_ROOT / _path
  33→    if str(_candidate) not in sys.path:
  34→        sys.path.insert(0, str(_candidate))
  35→
  36→from packages.contracts.workbench_contracts.protocol_v3 import (  # noqa: E402
  37→    ChapterContractV2,
  38→)
  39→
  40→from app.protocol_workflow.registries.chapters import (  # noqa: E402
  41→    ChapterSkillManifest,
  42→    load_chapter_registry,
  43→)
  44→
  45→BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = "protocol-v3-chapter-batch.v1"
  46→REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION = "protocol-v3-chapter-registry.v1"
  47→
  48→_BATCH_REQUIRED_KEYS = (
  49→    "schema_version",
  50→    "generated_for",
  51→    "authority",
  52→    "template_id",
  53→    "template_sha256",
  54→    "fact_vocabulary",
  55→    "claim_vocabulary",
  56→    "coverage_roles",
  57→    "fixtures",
  58→)
  59→
  60→
  61→class AssemblyInputError(ValueError):
  62→    """Raised when the batch inputs are unusable; reported without traceback."""
  63→
  64→
  65→def _read_json(path: Path) -> dict:
  66→    try:
  67→        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  68→    except OSError as exc:
  69→        raise AssemblyInputError(f"cannot read {path}: {exc}") from exc
  70→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
  71→        raise AssemblyInputError(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
  72→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
  73→        raise AssemblyInputError(f"{path} must contain a JSON object")
  74→    return data
  75→
  76→
  77→def _load_batch_document(batch_path: Path) -> dict:
  78→    batch = _read_json(batch_path)
  79→    missing = [key for key in _BATCH_REQUIRED_KEYS if key not in batch]
  80→    if missing:
  81→        raise AssemblyInputError(
  82→            f"{batch_path} is missing batch keys: {missing}"
  83→        )
  84→    if batch["schema_version"] != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
  85→        raise AssemblyInputError(
  86→            f"{batch_path} schema_version must be {BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION!r}; "
  87→            f"got {batch['schema_version']!r}"
  88→        )
  89→    if not isinstance(batch["coverage_roles"], dict) or not batch["coverage_roles"]:
  90→        raise AssemblyInputError(
  91→            f"{batch_path} coverage_roles must be a non-empty object"
  92→        )
  93→    for key in ("fact_vocabulary", "claim_vocabulary", "fixtures"):
  94→        if not isinstance(batch[key], list):
  95→            raise AssemblyInputError(f"{batch_path} {key} must be a list")
  96→    return batch
  97→
  98→
  99→def _load_payload_dir(directory: Path, label: str, node_ids: dict) -> dict:
 100→    if not directory.is_dir():
 101→        raise AssemblyInputError(f"{label} directory does not exist: {directory}")
 102→    payloads = {}
 103→    for node_id in sorted(node_ids):
 104→        path = directory / f"{node_id}.json"
 105→        payloads[node_id] = _read_json(path)
 106→    if not payloads:
 107→        raise AssemblyInputError(f"{label} directory has no JSON files: {directory}")
 108→    return payloads
 109→
 110→
 111→def assemble_registry(
 112→    contracts_dir: str | Path,
 113→    skills_dir: str | Path,
 114→    batch_path: str | Path,
 115→) -> dict:
 116→    """Assemble and fail-closed validate one batch registry payload."""
 117→    contracts_dir = Path(contracts_dir)
 118→    skills_dir = Path(skills_dir)
 119→    batch_path = Path(batch_path)
 120→    batch = _load_batch_document(batch_path)
 121→    contract_payloads = _load_payload_dir(contracts_dir, "chapter_contracts", batch["coverage_roles"])
 122→    skill_payloads = _load_payload_dir(skills_dir, "chapter_skills", batch["coverage_roles"])
 123→
 124→    entries = []
 125→    for stem in sorted(contract_payloads):
 126→        contract = ChapterContractV2.model_validate(contract_payloads[stem])
 127→        if contract.semantic_node_id != stem:
 128→            raise AssemblyInputError(
 129→                f"{contracts_dir / stem}.json binds semantic_node_id "
 130→                f"{contract.semantic_node_id!r}; the file name must be the node id"
 131→            )
 132→        if stem not in skill_payloads:
 133→            raise AssemblyInputError(f"no companion skill manifest for {stem!r}")
 134→        skill = ChapterSkillManifest.model_validate(skill_payloads[stem])
 135→        coverage_role = batch["coverage_roles"].get(stem)
 136→        if coverage_role is None:
 137→            raise AssemblyInputError(
 138→                f"{batch_path} declares no coverage role for {stem!r}"
 139→            )
 140→        entries.append(
 141→            {
 142→                "node_id": stem,
 143→                "coverage_role": coverage_role,
 144→                "contract": json.loads(contract.model_dump_json()),
 145→                "skills": [json.loads(skill.model_dump_json())],
 146→            }
 147→        )
 148→
 149→    payload = {
 150→        "schema_version": REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 151→        "generated_for": batch["generated_for"],
 152→        "authority": batch["authority"],
 153→        "template_id": batch["template_id"],
 154→        "template_sha256": batch["template_sha256"],
 155→        "fact_vocabulary": list(batch["fact_vocabulary"]),
 156→        "claim_vocabulary": list(batch["claim_vocabulary"]),
 157→        "chapters": entries,
 158→        "fixtures": list(batch["fixtures"]),
 159→    }
 160→    load_chapter_registry(payload)
 161→    return payload
 162→
 163→
 164→def assemble_registries(contracts_dir, skills_dir, batch_paths) -> dict:
 165→    """Combine explicit batch slices; never overwrite duplicate chapter identities."""
 166→    documents = [assemble_registry(contracts_dir, skills_dir, path) for path in batch_paths]
 167→    if not documents:
 168→        raise AssemblyInputError("at least one batch is required")
 169→    combined = dict(documents[0])
 170→    for document in documents[1:]:
 171→        if any(document[key] != combined[key] for key in ("template_id", "template_sha256")):
 172→            raise AssemblyInputError("batches refer to different template identities")
 173→    for key in ("generated_for", "authority"):
 174→        combined[key] = "\n".join(dict.fromkeys(document[key] for document in documents))
 175→    for key in ("fact_vocabulary", "claim_vocabulary"):
 176→        combined[key] = sorted({value for document in documents for value in document[key]})
 177→    for key in ("chapters", "fixtures"):
 178→        combined[key] = [value for document in documents for value in document[key]]
 179→    load_chapter_registry(combined)
 180→    return combined
 181→
 182→
 183→def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
 184→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
 185→        prog="assemble_chapter_registry",
 186→        description=(
 187→            "Assemble authored chapter-contract/skill JSON files and a batch "
 188→            "fixture/vocabulary document into a validated chapter registry "
 189→            "printed on stdout (read-only; no writes, activation or promotion)."
 190→        ),
 191→    )
 192→    parser.add_argument("--contracts-dir", required=True)
 193→    parser.add_argument("--skills-dir", required=True)
 194→    parser.add_argument("--batch", required=True, action="append", help="repeat for each batch to include")
 195→    parser.add_argument("--indent", type=int, default=2)
 196→    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
 197→    try:
 198→        payload = assemble_registries(args.contracts_dir, args.skills_dir, args.batch)
 199→    except ValueError as exc:
 200→        print(f"assembly failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
 201→        return 2
 202→    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=args.indent))
 203→    return 0
 204→
 205→
 206→if __name__ == "__main__":
 207→    raise SystemExit(main())

 446→class ChapterRegistryDocument(BaseModel):
 447→    """Closed, versioned chapter registry document."""
 448→
 449→    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, str_strip_whitespace=True)
 450→
 451→    schema_version: Literal[CHAPTER_REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION]  # type: ignore[valid-type]
 452→    generated_for: NonEmptyText
 453→    authority: NonEmptyText
 454→    template_id: StableId
 455→    template_sha256: Sha256
 456→    fact_vocabulary: tuple[NonEmptyText, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
 457→    claim_vocabulary: tuple[NonEmptyText, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
 458→    chapters: tuple[ChapterEntry, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
 459→    fixtures: tuple[ChapterFixture, ...] = ()
 460→
 461→    @field_validator("fact_vocabulary", "claim_vocabulary")
 462→    @classmethod
 463→    def _vocab_closed(
 464→        cls, value: tuple[NonEmptyText, ...], info: Any
 465→    ) -> tuple[NonEmptyText, ...]:
 466→        if len(value) != len(set(value)):
 467→            raise ValueError(f"{info.field_name} must not contain duplicates")
 468→        return value
 469→
 470→    @model_validator(mode="after")
 471→    def _cross_document_identity(self) -> ChapterRegistryDocument:
 472→        node_ids = [entry.node_id for entry in self.chapters]
 473→        if len(node_ids) != len(set(node_ids)):
 474→            duplicates = sorted({nid for nid in node_ids if node_ids.count(nid) > 1})
 475→            raise ValueError(f"duplicate chapter node ids: {duplicates}")
 476→        contract_ids = [entry.contract.chapter_contract_id for entry in self.chapters]
 477→        if len(contract_ids) != len(set(contract_ids)):
 478→            duplicates = sorted({cid for cid in contract_ids if contract_ids.count(cid) > 1})
 479→            raise ValueError(f"duplicate chapter contract ids: {duplicates}")
 480→        skill_ids = [
 481→            skill.skill_id for entry in self.chapters for skill in entry.skills
 482→        ]
 483→        if len(skill_ids) != len(set(skill_ids)):
 484→            duplicates = sorted({sid for sid in skill_ids if skill_ids.count(sid) > 1})
 485→            raise ValueError(f"duplicate skill ids: {duplicates}")
 486→        for entry in self.chapters:
 487→            if entry.contract.template_id != self.template_id:
 488→                raise ValueError(
 489→                    f"chapter {entry.node_id!r} template_id differs from the registry"
 490→                )
 491→            if entry.contract.template_sha256 != self.template_sha256:
 492→                raise ValueError(
 493→                    f"chapter {entry.node_id!r} template_sha256 differs from the registry"
 494→                )
 495→        fixture_ids = [fixture.fixture_id for fixture in self.fixtures]
 496→        if len(fixture_ids) != len(set(fixture_ids)):
 497→            duplicates = sorted({fid for fid in fixture_ids if fixture_ids.count(fid) > 1})
 498→            raise ValueError(f"duplicate fixture ids: {duplicates}")
 499→        declared = set(contract_ids)
 500→        for fixture in self.fixtures:
 501→            if fixture.chapter_contract_id not in declared:
 502→                raise ValueError(
 503→                    f"fixture {fixture.fixture_id!r} binds unknown chapter contract "
 504→                    f"{fixture.chapter_contract_id!r}"
 505→                )
 506→        return self

 509→def _load_json(source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
 510→    if isinstance(source, Mapping):
 511→        return json.loads(json.dumps(dict(source), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True))
 512→    path = Path(source)
 513→    try:
 514→        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 515→    except OSError as exc:
 516→        raise ChapterRegistryError(f"chapter registry unreadable: {path}") from exc
 517→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
 518→        raise ChapterRegistryError(f"chapter registry is not valid JSON: {path}") from exc
 519→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
 520→        raise ChapterRegistryError(
 521→            f"chapter registry must be a JSON object; got {type(data).__name__}"
 522→        )
 523→    return data

 526→def load_chapter_registry(
 527→    source: str | Path | Mapping[str, Any],
 528→) -> ChapterRegistryDocument:
 529→    """Load and validate a chapter registry document fail-closed.
 530→
 531→    Raises :class:`ChapterRegistryError` (a ``ValueError``) for any closed-set,
 532→    schema-version, duplicate, identity-binding or vocabulary violation.
 533→    """
 534→    data = _load_json(source)
 535→    _scan_credentials(data, "chapter-registry")
 536→    try:
 537→        document = ChapterRegistryDocument.model_validate(data)
 538→    except ValidationError as exc:
 539→        raise ChapterRegistryError(
 540→            f"chapter registry failed closed: {exc}"
 541→        ) from exc
 542→    return document

```python
def _reference_closure(fact_paths):
    """Independent naive closure over the raw accepted JSON (no module code)."""
    payload = json.loads(REAL_REGISTRY_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    members = collections.defaultdict(set)
    reaches = collections.defaultdict(set)   # upstream -> dependents
    for chapter in payload["chapters"]:
        contract_id = chapter["contract"]["chapter_contract_id"]
        for requirement in chapter["contract"]["substantive_content"]["fact_requirements"]:
            members[requirement["fact_path"]].add(contract_id)
        for rule in chapter["contract"].get("conditional_applicability_rules", []):
            for path in rule["triggering_fact_paths"]:
                members[path].add(contract_id)
            for path in rule["required_when_active_fact_paths"]:
                members[path].add(contract_id)
        for dependency in chapter["contract"].get("dependency_ids", []):
            reaches[dependency].add(contract_id)
    links = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for path, carriers in members.items():
        ordered = sorted(carriers)
        for left, right in itertools.combinations(ordered, 2):
            links[left].add(right)
            links[right].add(left)
    affected = {cid for path in fact_paths for cid in members[path]}
    frontier = set(affected)
    while frontier:
        discovered = set()
        for contract_id in sorted(frontier):
            discovered |= (links[contract_id] | reaches[contract_id]) - affected
        affected |= discovered
        frontier = discovered
    return affected
```

def _reference_closure(fact_paths: tuple[str, ...]) -> set[str]:

        content = chapter["contract"]["substantive_content"]
        for requirement in content["fact_requirements"]:
            carriers[requirement["fact_path"]].add(contract_id)
        for rule in chapter["contract"].get("conditional_applicability_rules", []):
            for path in rule["triggering_fact_paths"]:
                carriers[path].add(contract_id)
            for path in rule["required_when_active_fact_paths"]:
                carriers[path].add(contract_id)
        for dependency in chapter["contract"].get("dependency_ids", []):
            dependents[dependency].add(contract_id)
    links: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for carriers_for_fact in carriers.values():
        for left, right in itertools.combinations(sorted(carriers_for_fact), 2):
            links[left].add(right)
            links[right].add(left)
    affected = {cid for path in fact_paths for cid in carriers[path]}
    frontier = set(affected)
    while frontier:
        discovered: set[str] = set()
        for contract_id in sorted(frontier):
            discovered |= (links[contract_id] | dependents[contract_id]) - affected
        affected |= discovered
        frontier = discovered
    return affected

def test_hard_scheduling_cycle_rejected():
    shared = (("test.fact.shared", "required"),)
    cyclic = _registry(
        [
            _chapter(
                "v2_t_a",
                facts=shared,
                deps=("contract:v2-t-c:v2",),
                repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_a", ("contract:v2-t-c:v2",)),
            ),
            _chapter(
                "v2_t_b",
                facts=shared,
                deps=("contract:v2-t-a:v2",),
                repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_b", ("contract:v2-t-a:v2",)),
            ),
            _chapter(
                "v2_t_c",
                facts=shared,
                deps=("contract:v2-t-b:v2",),
                repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_c", ("contract:v2-t-b:v2",)),
            ),
        ]
    )
    document = load_chapter_registry(cyclic)
    with pytest.raises(DependencyGraphError) as excinfo:
        build_dependency_graph(document)
    message = str(excinfo.value)
    assert "scheduling cycle" in message
    for contract_id in (
        "contract:v2-t-a:v2",
        "contract:v2-t-b:v2",
        "contract:v2-t-c:v2",
    ):
        assert contract_id in message

    # Reciprocal shared-fact links must never be used as a cycle workaround:
    # the same three chapters with the closing hard edge removed build fine and
    # carry consistency edges on every pair.
    acyclic = _registry(
        [
            _chapter(
                "v2_t_a",
                facts=shared,
                deps=("contract:v2-t-c:v2",),
                repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_a", ("contract:v2-t-c:v2",)),
            ),
            _chapter(
                "v2_t_b",
                facts=shared,
                deps=("contract:v2-t-a:v2",),
                repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_b", ("contract:v2-t-a:v2",)),
            ),
            _chapter("v2_t_c", facts=shared),
        ]
    )
    graph = build_dependency_graph(load_chapter_registry(acyclic))
    assert graph.findings == ()
    assert _edge_pairs(graph, EdgeKind.SCHEDULING) == {
        ("contract:v2-t-c:v2", "contract:v2-t-a:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-b:v2"),
    }
    assert _edge_pairs(graph, EdgeKind.CONSISTENCY_IMPACT) == {
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-b:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-c:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-b:v2", "contract:v2-t-c:v2"),
    }


def test_reciprocal_consistency_links_are_legal_and_create_no_false_cycle():
    document = load_chapter_registry(
        _registry(
            [
                _chapter(
                    "v2_t_a",
                    facts=(("test.fact.shared", "required"),),
                    deps=("contract:v2-t-b:v2",),
                    repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_a", ("contract:v2-t-b:v2",)),
                ),
                _chapter(
                    "v2_t_b",
                    facts=(
                        ("test.fact.shared", "required"),
                        ("test.fact.beta", "optional"),
                    ),
                ),
                _chapter(
                    "v2_t_c",
                    facts=(("test.fact.shared", "required"),),
                    deps=("contract:v2-t-a:v2",),
                    repair_policy=_policy("v2_t_c", ("contract:v2-t-a:v2",)),
                ),
            ]
        )
    )
    graph = build_dependency_graph(document)
    assert graph.findings == ()

    scheduling = _edge_pairs(graph, EdgeKind.SCHEDULING)
    assert scheduling == {
        ("contract:v2-t-b:v2", "contract:v2-t-a:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-c:v2"),
    }
    consistency = {
        (edge.left_contract_id, edge.right_contract_id): edge
        for edge in graph.edges
        if edge.kind is EdgeKind.CONSISTENCY_IMPACT
    }
    assert set(consistency) == {
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-b:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-c:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-b:v2", "contract:v2-t-c:v2"),
    }
    for edge in consistency.values():
        assert edge.reciprocal is True
        assert edge.shared_fact_paths == ("test.fact.shared",)
    # The pair carrying both a hard edge and a reciprocal clinical link stays
    # legal: the consistency link never enters the scheduling DAG.
    order = graph.topological_order()
    assert len(order) == 3
    assert order.index("contract:v2-t-b:v2") < order.index("contract:v2-t-a:v2")
    assert order.index("contract:v2-t-a:v2") < order.index("contract:v2-t-c:v2")


def test_missing_repair_owner_and_unknown_target_are_identified():
    document = load_chapter_registry(
        _registry(
            [
                _chapter("v2_t_a", facts=(("test.fact.alpha", "required"),)),
                _chapter(
                    "v2_t_b",
                    facts=(("test.fact.beta", "required"),),
                    deps=("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-ghost:v2"),
                    repair_policy=_policy(
                        "v2_t_b", ("contract:v2-t-ghost:v2",), owner="ai"
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )
    )
    graph = build_dependency_graph(document)

    assert {finding.code for finding in graph.findings} == {
        "missing_repair_owner",
        "unknown_dependency_target",
    }
    assert all(finding.severity == "error" for finding in graph.findings)
    ownerless = next(
        finding
        for finding in graph.findings
        if finding.code == "missing_repair_owner"
    )
    assert ownerless.location == "contract:v2-t-a:v2->contract:v2-t-b:v2"
    unknown = next(
        finding
        for finding in graph.findings
        if finding.code == "unknown_dependency_target"
    )
    assert unknown.location == "contract:v2-t-b:v2->contract:v2-t-ghost:v2"

    # Identified, never silently dropped: both declared hard edges survive.
    scheduling = {
        edge.upstream_contract_id: edge
        for edge in graph.edges
        if edge.kind is EdgeKind.SCHEDULING
    }
    assert set(scheduling) == {"contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-ghost:v2"}
    assert scheduling["contract:v2-t-a:v2"].repair_owner is None
    assert scheduling["contract:v2-t-ghost:v2"].repair_owner == "ai"
    assert _edge_pairs(graph, EdgeKind.SCHEDULING) == {
        ("contract:v2-t-a:v2", "contract:v2-t-b:v2"),
        ("contract:v2-t-ghost:v2", "contract:v2-t-b:v2"),
    }
    # The dangling target is not a registry carrier and is never invented.
    report = graph.impact(["test.fact.beta"])
    assert report.affected_contract_ids == ("contract:v2-t-b:v2",)
    assert report.findings == graph.findings
    assert all(node.contract_id != "contract:v2-t-ghost:v2" for node in graph.nodes)


def test_unrelated_chapters_remain_stable(real_graph):
    document = load_chapter_registry(
        _registry(
            [
                _chapter("v2_t_a", facts=(("test.fact.alpha", "required"),)),
                _chapter("v2_t_b", facts=(("test.fact.alpha", "required"),)),
                _chapter("v2_t_c", facts=(("test.fact.gamma", "required"),)),
                _chapter("v2_t_d", facts=(("test.fact.gamma", "required"),)),
            ]
        )
    )
    graph = build_dependency_graph(document)
    projection_before = graph.projection_sha256()
    report = graph.impact(["test.fact.alpha"])
    assert report.affected_contract_ids == (
        "contract:v2-t-a:v2",
        "contract:v2-t-b:v2",
    )
    assert report.affects("contract:v2-t-c:v2") is False
    assert report.affects("contract:v2-t-d:v2") is False
    second = graph.impact(["test.fact.gamma"])
    assert second.affected_contract_ids == (
        "contract:v2-t-c:v2",
        "contract:v2-t-d:v2",
    )
    assert second.affects("contract:v2-t-a:v2") is False
    assert second.affects("contract:v2-t-b:v2") is False
    assert graph.projection_sha256() == projection_before
    assert graph.contracts_for_fact("test.fact.gamma") == (
        "contract:v2-t-c:v2",
        "contract:v2-t-d:v2",
    )

    # Accepted registry: a chapter-unique fact moves exactly one chapter.
    isolated = real_graph.impact([ISOLATED_FACT_PATH])
    assert isolated.affected_contract_ids == (ISOLATED_FACT_CONTRACT,)
    assert isolated.affects(UNRELATED_TO_ISOLATED) is False
    assert isolated.affects("contract:v2-n-11-1:v2") is False
    assert real_graph.projection_sha256() == real_graph.projection_sha256()


def test_broad_dose_endpoint_change_returns_every_affected_chapter_without_truncation(
    real_graph,
):
    for fact_path, direct_size, expected_affected in BROAD_FACT_CASES:
        direct = real_graph.contracts_for_fact(fact_path)
        report = real_graph.impact([fact_path])
        assert len(direct) == direct_size
        assert set(direct) < set(report.affected_contract_ids)
        assert len(report.affected_contract_ids) == expected_affected
        assert report.affected_contract_ids == tuple(
            sorted(report.affected_contract_ids)
        )
        assert len(report.affected_contract_ids) == len(
            set(report.affected_contract_ids)
        )
        # Complete set: equal to an independent naive closure over the raw JSON.
        assert set(report.affected_contract_ids) == _reference_closure((fact_path,))
        # Every affected chapter is classified exactly once (no omission).
        assert (
            len(report.direct_contract_ids)
            + len(report.consistency_contract_ids)
            + len(report.scheduling_contract_ids)
            == len(report.affected_contract_ids)
        )
        assert len(report.scheduling_contract_ids) > 0


def test_same_fact_update_has_a_single_adoption_effect(real_graph):
    first = real_graph.impact(["picos.primary_endpoint"])
    second = real_graph.impact(["picos.primary_endpoint"])
    assert first == second
    assert first.impact_sha256 == second.impact_sha256

    # The same fact update expressed twice / in another order is one adoption.
    duplicated = real_graph.impact(
        ["picos.primary_endpoint", "picos.primary_endpoint"]
    )
    assert duplicated.changed_fact_paths == ("picos.primary_endpoint",)
    assert duplicated.impact_sha256 == first.impact_sha256

    # Graph rendering is a projection, not a second editable store: reading it
    # never mutates the graph and a rebuilt graph adopts the same state.
    projection_before = real_graph.projection_sha256()
    real_graph.impact(["picos.intervention_dose_regimen"])
    assert real_graph.projection_sha256() == projection_before
    rebuilt = build_dependency_graph(REAL_REGISTRY_PATH)
    assert rebuilt.registry_sha256 == real_graph.registry_sha256
    assert rebuilt.impact(["picos.primary_endpoint"]).impact_sha256 == (
        first.impact_sha256
    )

    # A combined update is the union of the single-fact adoptions.
    dose = real_graph.impact(["picos.intervention_dose_regimen"])
    combined = real_graph.impact(
        ["picos.primary_endpoint", "picos.intervention_dose_regimen"]
    )
    assert set(combined.affected_contract_ids) == set(
        first.affected_contract_ids
    ) | set(dose.affected_contract_ids)
    assert len(combined.affected_contract_ids) > len(first.affected_contract_ids)

    # The module keeps no editable store: its value objects are frozen.
    with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
        real_graph.nodes = ()
    with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
        real_graph.impact(["picos.primary_endpoint"]).affected_contract_ids = ()

def test_typed_edges_keep_the_three_relationship_kinds_distinct(real_graph):
    kinds = {edge.kind for edge in real_graph.edges}
    assert kinds == {
        EdgeKind.FACT_MEMBERSHIP,
        EdgeKind.SCHEDULING,
        EdgeKind.CONSISTENCY_IMPACT,
    }

    payload = json.loads(REAL_REGISTRY_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    declared_pairs = set()
    carriers = 0
    for chapter in payload["chapters"]:
        contract = chapter["contract"]
        if contract.get("dependency_ids"):
            carriers += 1
        for dependency in contract.get("dependency_ids", []):
            declared_pairs.add(
                (dependency, contract["chapter_contract_id"])
            )
    assert carriers == ACCEPTED_DEPENDENT_CARRIER_COUNT
    # Scheduling admits explicit dependency_ids only; no cross-reference is
    # promoted into a hard edge.
    assert _edge_pairs(real_graph, EdgeKind.SCHEDULING) == declared_pairs
    assert len(declared_pairs) == ACCEPTED_SCHEDULING_EDGE_COUNT
    assert len(_edge_pairs(real_graph, EdgeKind.CONSISTENCY_IMPACT)) == (
        ACCEPTED_CONSISTENCY_EDGE_COUNT
    )
    # endpoint/estimand/statistics style reciprocity: the four carriers of the
    # primary endpoint fact produce six reciprocal consistency pairs.
    endpoint_pairs = [
        edge
        for edge in real_graph.edges
        if edge.kind is EdgeKind.CONSISTENCY_IMPACT
        and "picos.primary_endpoint" in edge.shared_fact_paths
    ]
    assert len(endpoint_pairs) == 6
    assert all(edge.reciprocal for edge in endpoint_pairs)


def test_accepted_registry_graph_is_complete_acyclic_and_error_free(real_graph):
    assert real_graph.findings == ()
    assert len(real_graph.nodes) == ACCEPTED_NODE_COUNT
    node_ids = {node.contract_id for node in real_graph.nodes}
    assert len(node_ids) == ACCEPTED_NODE_COUNT
    for edge in real_graph.scheduling_edges:
        assert edge.dependent_contract_id in node_ids
        assert edge.upstream_contract_id in node_ids
        assert edge.repair_owner in {"ai", "user", "system"}
    for membership in real_graph.memberships:
        assert membership.contract_id in node_ids
    order = real_graph.topological_order()
    assert len(order) == ACCEPTED_NODE_COUNT
    position = {contract_id: index for index, contract_id in enumerate(order)}
    for edge in real_graph.scheduling_edges:
        assert position[edge.upstream_contract_id] < position[edge.dependent_contract_id]

    assert CONDITIONAL_TRIGGER_ONLY_CONTRACT in trigger_report.affected_contract_ids

```python
"""Registry-level typed dependency / impact graph for Protocol v3 (Task 3R.4).

This module is registry infrastructure only: it indexes the accepted
:class:`ChapterRegistryDocument` into an explicit, typed edge structure and
computes deterministic impact sets.  It authors no clinical content, decides no
medical or QC judgment, calls no product model and writes nothing.

Three relationship kinds stay explicitly typed and separate:

``fact_membership``
    A chapter declares fact paths in ``fact_requirements`` (required, optional
    or forbidden) and in ``conditional_applicability_rules`` (both the
    triggering paths and the when-active obligations).  Both unconditional and
    conditional paths are indexed; a conditional-only path is a first-class
    change target.

``scheduling``
    ONLY explicit ``ChapterContractV2.dependency_ids`` become hard/order edges
    of the scheduling DAG (upstream dependency -> dependent chapter).  Cross
    references, shared facts or chapter numbering are never promoted into a
    scheduling edge.

``consistency_impact``
    Reciprocal clinical relationships (summary/body, SoA/assessments,
    endpoint/estimand/statistics, dose/design/population) are derived from
    shared fact membership and kept outside the scheduling DAG, so they can
    never fabricate a scheduling cycle -- and a real hard cycle is never
    hidden behind a reciprocal link.

Impact computation returns every affected chapter without truncation: the seed
is the set of chapters that declare a changed path, the closure adds the
reciprocal consistency neighbours (transitively) and the downstream chapters
of the scheduling DAG in dependency order.

Purity / CAS declaration
------------------------
``build_dependency_graph`` and ``DependencyGraph.impact`` are pure functions of
(accepted registry, changed material facts).  The module keeps no store, no
cache and no module-level mutable state: impact is recomputed from immutable
frozen inputs and yields the same identified set and the same
``impact_sha256`` adoption key for the same fact update.  ``projection()`` /
``projection_sha256()`` render the graph as a read-only projection of the
accepted registry; the rendering is not a new authority and never a second
editable store.  Project-confirmation invalidation therefore uses the changed
material facts and the reported affected set, never a blanket reopen-all.
"""
```

 327→            )
 328→        dependents: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
 329→        known = set(self.contract_ids())
 330→        for edge in self.scheduling_edges:

- Impact algorithm. Seeds = chapters declaring any changed path; then a deterministic level-BFS closure adds reciprocal consistency neighbours (undirected, transitive) and scheduling dependents (downstream only, following the DAG), repeating to a fixed point. Classification = the relation by which a chapter first entered the set, so `direct + consistency + scheduling` is an exact partition of the affected set.
